case_number: Criminal Appeal No. of 2022 (Arising out of Special Leave Petition (Criminal) No. 2872 of 2022)
summary: The appeal challenged the Karnataka High Court's dismissal of a criminal revision petition upholding conviction under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, for dishonour of a cheque. The Trial Court had imposed a fine and directed interim compensation under Section 143A, which the appellant failed to pay, leading to denial of right to cross-examine the complainant. The Appellate and High Courts upheld the conviction, citing non-compliance with interim payment. The Supreme Court examined whether non-payment of interim compensation under Section 143A(1) could lawfully result in denial of the right to cross-examine. It held that the statutory mechanism under Section 143A(5) permits recovery of interim compensation as a fine but does not authorize curtailing of statutory or constitutional rights like fair trial. Denial of cross-examination solely due to non-payment of interim compensation is impermissible, as the statute prescribes specific remedies for non-compliance. The courts below erred in linking procedural compliance with substantive rights.
legal_provisions_cited: State of Uttar Pradesh vs. Singhara Singh and others
final_judgment: The appeal is allowed. The judgments and orders of the High Court and lower courts denying the right to cross-examine solely on account of non-payment of interim compensation under Section 143A are set aside. The matter is remanded to the Trial Court to allow the appellant a reasonable opportunity to cross-examine the complainant, in accordance with law.
